protocol: D-000 new cycle, turn 1 of 3; refute not confirm; two severable PREFERENCE-LADEN Route B selections in D-028 form
summary: Both cited digests match live bytes, and every named attack fails on the operative clauses. The pair is genuinely severable -- separate Subjects, Decisions, Alternatives, Readiness lines, Reversibility lines and overturn commits, with D-047 expressly rejecting 'Bundle with D-048 as one unsverable act' by the D-025 defect. Neither entry writes a disposition, marks anything SATISFIED, claims condition-1 discharge, treats section31 v4 as the Phase-1A packet, or makes the coordinator a recording authority -- on that last point both go further than D-028 by adding that independent review is required and a coordinator-composed SATISFIED is unlawful under DR-204. One SHOULD-FIX blocks CONSENT, and it is an asymmetry inside the draft rather than a disagreement with the precedent: D-047's Reversibility carries D-028's full form including the dependent-disposition limb, and D-048's drops it, reading only 'Total before dependents. Overturn: C-D048.' The correct wording sits forty lines above it in the same file.

objections.location: D-048 Reversibility (draft line 98), against D-047's Reversibility (lines 57-59) and adopted D-028
objections.claim: D-048 declares reversibility that is conditional on dependents and then supplies only a bare commit reference, dropping the limb that says what an overturn after a dependent disposition actually requires. Its sibling in the same draft carries that limb in full.
evidence: D-048 reads in full: 'Total before dependents. Overturn: C-D048.'
D-047 reads: 'Total before any dependent disposition lands. After one lands, overturn also requires that disposition's owning-authority supersession. Overturn: C-D047.'

Adopted D-028, which the measured-inputs table names as 'the form this pair copies', reads: 'total before any dependent disposition lands. After one lands, overturn also requires that disposition's owning-authority supersession.'
So the second limb exists in the precedent and in the sibling entry, and is absent only from D-048.
objections.whyItMatters: 'Total before dependents' is a conditional class, and the condition is exactly the case where a bare revert is insufficient: once an owner-recorded disposition depends on the selection, overturning also requires that disposition's owning-authority supersession. Without the limb, someone executing an overturn of D-048 from its own text reverts C-D048 and stops, in the one scenario the class exists to flag. D-000 clause 3 makes the overturn procedure a mandatory element, and the corpus writes it out for conditional-class entries precisely because the class alone is not the procedure.
objections.aggravatingCircumstance: This is not a case of the corpus having to be consulted. The correct sentence is in the same document, forty lines earlier, on the entry immediately above it, for an identically classed act. Whatever process produced the asymmetry did not compare the pair against itself.
objections.whyThisSeverity: The same severity I gave C2-D046-01, which was the identical defect -- a reversibility line stating the class while omitting the limb that makes a conditional overturn actionable. It is not a MUST-FIX: nothing stated is false, the class declaration is correct, and no authority is created or discharged by the omission.
objections.remedy: Give D-048 D-047's sentence: 'Total before any dependent disposition lands. After one lands, overturn also requires that disposition's owning-authority supersession. Overturn: C-D048.'

whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: a352d08dc51e3275a90e7d09f450c0a396a41d00eb3aac107d7cdef257950b61 both times, matching the dispatch. No drift.

The attack 'cited digests do not match live bytes' fails on both. COORD 37c375df54b0cb652e9e6949aa27936462ce92ae7395b71b460d5c6d54acbfdf and file 08 6547e6ace2ae61e664af0f65059b66c2cb3d0539d64f6687aba04f8f54dc4cd7, each measured by me against live bytes. The file-08 pin is the current post-SATISFIED-re-record value from f6d9401, not a carried-forward stale one.

The form claim is accurate, checked against the adopted precedent rather than accepted. D-028 carries: Subject as a single row; the owning V1 authority named from file 08; 'Select Route B … architecture preview only'; preview scope with what remains owed; coordinator selects / named owners record / coordinator may draft / D-000 does not make the coordinator those authorities; writes no disposition; marks nothing SATISFIED; 'A completed, reviewed, owner-recorded disposition may discharge condition 1 for DR-005 within its preview scope'; conditions 2-5 remain; condition 5 the only authorization for docs/v2/implementation/; alternatives; readiness zero at adoption; and the two-limb reversibility. D-047 reproduces every element. D-048 reproduces every element except the reversibility limb above.

Both entries go beyond D-028 on the axis that matters most here, which the dispatch names as 'coordinator becomes recording authority'. Where D-028 says 'D-000 does not make the coordinator those authorities', D-047 and D-048 each add 'Independent review is required. A coordinator-composed SATISFIED is unlawful (DR-204).' That is a real strengthening and it is correctly attributed -- DR-204's adjudication of DR-001's 2026-08-12 SATISFIED as provenance-UNLAWFUL is the source I verified during the SATISFIED-grade cycle.

The attack 'unsverable bundle (D-025 defect)' fails. The two entries carry separate Subject lines (DR-002 only; DR-004 only), separate owning authorities, separate Decision blocks, separate Alternatives, separate Readiness effect lines, separate Reversibility lines, and separate overturn commits C-D047 and C-D048. The header states 'Two severable entries', and D-047's alternatives expressly reject 'Bundle with D-048 as one unsverable act. Rejected: D-025 defect.'
The attack 'writes a disposition in this entry' fails: clause 5 of each reads 'Writes no disposition', and the header states '**Does not** write dispositions.'

The attack 'silent SATISFIED or condition-1 discharge' fails on both limbs. SATISFIED appears only in refusals -- the header's '**Does not** mark SATISFIED', clause 5's 'Marks nothing SATISFIED', and clause 4's 'A coordinator-composed SATISFIED is unlawful (DR-204)'. Condition 1 is never claimed discharged: the construction is conditional and future and row-scoped, 'A completed, reviewed, owner-recorded disposition may discharge condition 1 for DR-002 within the scope it names', which is D-028's own construction with 'within its preview scope' rendered as 'within the scope it names'.

The attack 'treats section31 v4 as the Phase-1A packet' fails twice in D-048: clause 3 states 'The eight-bullet Phase-1A packet remains owed on the authoritative path. This entry writes no Phase-1A packet and does not discharge that obligation. D-043 / D-045 recorded the §3.1 binding instrument; that instrument is not the packet', and the alternatives reject 'Treat section31 v4 as the Phase-1A packet. Rejected: D-045.' That matches what I graded at the v4 review, where the instrument reports one bound item of eight and expressly refuses to be the packet.

The attack 'condition 5 / docs/v2/implementation' fails: both clause 5s state 'Condition 5 remains the only implementation authorization', and both add 'Authorizes no blueprint', which D-028 does not carry.

The attack 'file 08 edited' fails: git reports the whole of docs/v2/architecture/, COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md and the freeze clean, with zero modified tracked files. The draft is pre-adoption and has changed nothing.

The D-037 characterization is accurate. The measured-inputs table says 'adopted; consume file 11 via D-001 A/B/C. This is Route B.' Adopted D-037's decision-type line reads 'Restates file 08's only-checklist rule, file 07/10 competing-list disclaimers, file 11's header, and D-001 A/B/C. Adds no fourth route.' Selecting Route B is therefore consumption through an existing route rather than a new one.

The rows' standing is unchanged and the draft does not imply otherwise: DR-002 remains HARD-BLOCKED with AC-2 satisfied and DR-004 remains HARD-BLOCKED in live file 08, and neither entry asserts a standing change.

Examined and declined: each entry's clause 2 enumerates the rows it does not select, and neither list covers DR-009 or DR-010, both of which carry condition-1 routes in D-001 (A and C respectively). I decline this because the enumeration is an addition D-028 does not require -- D-028 relies on 'Subject: DR-005 only' alone -- and because the operative sentence here is categorical: 'This selection is one row.' An incomplete illustrative list behind a categorical statement does not create an implication that the unlisted rows are selected.

Examined and declined: D-047's alternatives carry the anti-bundling rejection and D-048's do not. One statement of the rejection covers the pair, the header independently declares severability, and each entry has its own overturn commit. Recording it so the asymmetry is visible as examined rather than missed.
whatIDidNotCheck: The Codex review of this subject. Not read; the file is confirmed absent at review time.

Adopted D-029 and D-030, which the header also cites as form precedents. The measured-inputs table names D-028 as 'the form this pair copies', so I compared against D-028 in full and did not re-derive the other two.

Whether the Evidence authority, the V1 coordinator, and the Evidence/retention authority named as owners are the owners file 08 currently records for DR-002 and DR-004. I read the rows' status cells for standing; I did not extract and compare the owner cells.

Whether Route B is the right preference for these two rows. That is the PREFERENCE-LADEN judgement the entries exist to make and the alternatives state the rejected option ('Leave on full Route A. Reachable'); a reviewer refuting rather than confirming can test that the choice is disclosed and reversible, which it is, not that it is correct.
What a future owner-recorded disposition under either selection would contain. Both entries expressly write none, and the conditional clause 5 is the only thing said about their effect.

nonConsentNote: I do not CONSENT, on one SHOULD-FIX, and the pair is otherwise well built. Severability is real rather than asserted, both digests are current rather than carried forward, and on the coordinator-authority axis these entries are stronger than the precedent they copy. My objection is that the draft is not internally consistent with itself: two entries of the same class, drafted together, and only one states what an overturn requires once a dependent disposition exists. The fix is to copy the sentence already present on the entry above.
